title: Cross Cell Evaluation of Electrochemical Impedance Features for Lithium Ion Battery Remaining Useful Life Prediction
description: Evaluation of whether electrochemical impedance features transfer across lithium-ion cells. Electrolyte resistance Re and charge-transfer resistance Rct are read directly from the recorded impedance fields of the NASA dataset (B0005, B0006, B0007, B0018) with no circuit fitting. Between-cell variation is assessed with linear mixed-effects models because cycle-level measurements within a cell are strongly autocorrelated: intraclass correlation is 0.899 for Re and 0.854 for Rct against 0.646 for capacity, with eta-squared of 0.600, 0.480 and 0.038. A complete four-fold leave-one-battery-out random forest gives a mean RMSE of 19.05 cycles (range 5.13 to 32.24) and mean R-squared of 0.668. A feature ablation shows this is carried by the capacity trajectory: Re and Rct alone reach 33.20 cycles with mean R-squared of -0.020, while a training-free linear extrapolation of capacity reaches 22.19 cycles. Impedance features therefore discriminate strongly between cells but transfer poorly as RUL predictors. This release corrects reporting errors in v1.0.0 and v2.0.0 and discloses the impedance-to-cycle mapping; see CHANGELOG.md.
